name: Workbench P005 native Windows Goals and helper shutdown regression
summary: 32 native assertions passed: 16 owned-helper framing/lifetime checks including an actual Windows TerminateProcess error 5 after exit, plus 16 interactive WPF Goal controls and clean resident shutdown. The historical failure did not capture post-error child liveness; the deterministic regression proves and guards the exit-race defect class, while a live-helper access-denied control still fails.

prerequisites.runtime: Native Windows PowerShell/.NET Framework; signed-in interactive Session1 for WPF. SSH is control transport only.
prerequisites.custody: Five remote Get-FileHash values matched current canonical local bytes before this evidence was created.
prerequisites.selection: Fixture-owned helper processes and Goal state; no real operator Goal writes.

assertions.evidence: Actual Win32 TerminateProcess on the exited owned helper returns code5; the guard rechecks exit and completes.
The same code5 while a real owned helper remains alive propagates. Unrelated code6 also propagates.
All16 WPF controls pass and the InteractiveToken process exits0 after disposing the resident host.

rootCauseVerification.hypothesis: The cleanup boundary fails to handle Win32 access-denied after the owned process exits between its running check and termination.
rootCauseVerification.alternativeHypothesis: The termination error indicates a still-running process whose termination is genuinely denied.
rootCauseVerification.distinguishingTest: Maintained native fixture holds one child alive for injected code5 and verifies propagation; then exits that same child between the running check and native TerminateProcess, observes actual code5, and verifies safe completion.
rootCauseVerification.actualObservation: The live denial propagated with the child still alive; actual TerminateProcess returned5 after child exit and was handled; Goals resident shutdown exited0.
rootCauseVerification.historicalLimit: The original failure stack did not capture child liveness after its failed Kill, so its exact race timing is not retrospectively proven.

harnessCorrection: The first new fixture used Process.Kill after WaitForExit, which is an idempotent no-op once .NET caches exit. It was corrected to call the same native TerminateProcess primitive with the retained owned handle.
limits: Current-build native fixtures only; exact installed-artifact acceptance across all three OSes remains pending.
New actual PUI native-goal operator integration remains pending.
